items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: And it was a great band. Mark Johnson was playing bass and he was, at that time, auditioning for the job of Bill Evans, which he got. John Riley was playing drums

ctx.x: It was Bill Byrne who was the trumpet. He was the band manager. And he called — well let me preface the story, I was playing on Long Island with, well it was called the Long Island Jazz Quintet at this time. This was 1978. And it was Glen Drews who was playing trumpet, actually he’s the one that got called to play with Woody first. So Glen Drews the trumpet player, he left our group and he was on Woody’s band. And a couple of months later the phone rang and it was Bill Byrne, who was the road manager and the…

was like “Four Brothers” boom. Early on, here we go. And it was a great band. Mark Johnson was playing bass and he was, at that time, auditioning for the job of Bill Evans, which he got. John Riley was playing drums who now is playing in the Vanguard Jazz Orchestra sitting in Mel Lewis’ seat, Frank Tiberi of course, Dave LaLama, Ralph’s brother on piano. It was really an incredible band. And the other thing that struck me about Woody that was really inspiring was how forward thinking he was. He didn’t live in the…
What would have got you fired from the Woody Herman band? Not you in particular, but did he have —
